<p id="S4.SS1.p6.1" class="ltx_p">Rubric-based and free-form trust share the update of Eq. (<a href="#S4.E5" title="In 4.1 Trust Assessment ‣ 4 The TASMAN Framework ‣ Knowing Whom to Trust is not Enough: The Trust–Agreement Gap in Repeated Multi-Party LLM Negotiation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5</span></a>) and differ only in how <math id="S4.SS1.p6.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="z_{ij}^{e}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>z</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow><mi>e</mi></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">z_{ij}^{e}</annotation></semantics></math> is produced, so comparing them isolates whether a predefined rubric yields better trust estimates than criteria the LLM constructs itself.
BRS differs from both in how evidence becomes trust and in how past evidence is discounted, so comparisons with BRS evaluate each method as a whole rather than a single design choice (RQ2).</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">4.2 </span>Agent Roles and Decisions</h3>

<div id="S4.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S4.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The parties differ only in their role instructions; proposing, voting, and trust assessment are identical for all.
A <em id="S4.SS2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">general</em> (G) agent is agreement-oriented: it pursues its private preferences but treats any deal clearing its BATNA and preserving its main priorities as a success.
A <em id="S4.SS2.p1.1.2" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">hard-bargaining</em> (HB) agent sets a higher bar than its BATNA and concedes only after accumulating evidence that the present parties are unlikely to offer more, so trust can change both whether and when it settles.
The <em id="S4.SS2.p1.1.3" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">adversarial</em> agent in <math id="S4.SS2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{B}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℬ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{B}</annotation></semantics></math> presents a plausible party identity while privately preferring that no agreement is reached; it may block directly or selectively, but must keep its public explanations consistent with its cover identity.
We include all the prompts in Appendix <a href="#A6" title="Appendix F Prompts ‣ Knowing Whom to Trust is not Enough: The Trust–Agreement Gap in Repeated Multi-Party LLM Negotiation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">F</span></a>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS2.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S4.SS2.p2.1" class="ltx_p">At decision time, a proposer receives its current trust in every other party, and a voter receives its trust in the current proposer.
The model weighs trust against its private utility, the current deal, and the recent history on its own.
We vary the amount of guidance on how to use trust as an experimental factor (Section <a href="#S5" title="5 Experiments and Results ‣ Knowing Whom to Trust is not Enough: The Trust–Agreement Gap in Repeated Multi-Party LLM Negotiation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5</span></a>).
This design keeps trust an object of behavioral study: any difference between trust-aware and trust-agnostic agents reflects how the models themselves take trust up in their reasoning.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S5" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">5 </span>Experiments and Results</h2>

<div id="S5.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Each episode instantiates the game of Section <a href="#S3" title="3 Problem Formulation ‣ Knowing Whom to Trust is not Enough: The Trust–Agreement Gap in Repeated Multi-Party LLM Negotiation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a> with five parties, five issues, and four options per issue.
An episode lasts at most <math id="S5.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="L_{e}=15" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>L</mi><mi>e</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>15</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">L_{e}=15</annotation></semantics></math> rounds, so each party proposes at most three times, and each trajectory consists of <math id="S5.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="E=20" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>E</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>20</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">E=20</annotation></semantics></math> distinct episodes with the same parties.
Each experimental run repeats these episodes in <math id="S5.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="10" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>10</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">10</annotation></semantics></math> seed-matched trajectories (Appendix <a href="#A5.SS1" title="E.1 Seed Generation ‣ Appendix E Additional Quantitative Results ‣ Knowing Whom to Trust is not Enough: The Trust–Agreement Gap in Repeated Multi-Party LLM Negotiation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">E.1</span></a>), and trajectories share the same proposer orders across conditions.
We evaluate two settings that differ in the honest population: two hard bargainers and two general agents (2HB+2G), our main setting, and one hard bargainer and three general agents (1HB+3G), which also uses <math id="S5.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="20" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>20</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">20</annotation></semantics></math> different episodes with different private utilities and thresholds (Appendix <a href="#A1.SS3" title="A.3 Why the 1HB+3G Set Requires Different Private Scores ‣ Appendix A Negotiation Scenario Generation ‣ Knowing Whom to Trust is not Enough: The Trust–Agreement Gap in Repeated Multi-Party LLM Negotiation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">A.3</span></a>), for <math id="S5.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="40" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>40</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">40</annotation></semantics></math> distinct episodes in total.
In both settings, a single adversary aims to prevent agreement, so its threshold exceeds the maximum attainable utility of <math id="S5.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="100" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>100</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">100</annotation></semantics></math>, whereas every scenario contains a deal that meets all honest parties’ BATNAs.
Appendix <a href="#A1" title="Appendix A Negotiation Scenario Generation ‣ Knowing Whom to Trust is not Enough: The Trust–Agreement Gap in Repeated Multi-Party LLM Negotiation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">A</span></a> describes the episode generation process in detail.</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S5.p2.1" class="ltx_p">We evaluate the six models in Table <a href="#S5.T1" title="Table 1 ‣ 5 Experiments and Results ‣ Knowing Whom to Trust is not Enough: The Trust–Agreement Gap in Repeated Multi-Party LLM Negotiation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a>, four reasoning (<span id="S5.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">r</span>), two non-reasoning (<span id="S5.p2.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">nr</span>); unless stated otherwise, all five parties use the same model.
All model calls use temperature <math id="S5.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.7" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.7</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.7</annotation></semantics></math> and at most <math id="S5.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="16{,}000" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>16,000</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">16{,}000</annotation></semantics></math> generated tokens.
Trust starts from the uninformed prior <math id="S5.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau_{ij}^{1}=0.5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>τ</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow><mn>1</mn></msubsup><mo>=</mo><mn>0.5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau_{ij}^{1}=0.5</annotation></semantics></math>, rubric-based and free-form updates use <math id="S5.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\lambda=0.7" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>λ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.7</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lambda=0.7</annotation></semantics></math> in Eq. (<a href="#S4.E5" title="In 4.1 Trust Assessment ‣ 4 The TASMAN Framework ‣ Knowing Whom to Trust is not Enough: The Trust–Agreement Gap in Repeated Multi-Party LLM Negotiation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5</span></a>), and BRS updates use <math id="S5.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\gamma=0.9" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>γ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.9</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\gamma=0.9</annotation></semantics></math>.
Trust can improve outcomes only when agents respect their threshold <math id="S5.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\beta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>β</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\beta</annotation></semantics></math> and baseline performance is not saturated.
Table <a href="#S5.T1" title="Table 1 ‣ 5 Experiments and Results ‣ Knowing Whom to Trust is not Enough: The Trust–Agreement Gap in Repeated Multi-Party LLM Negotiation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a> shows that the non-reasoning models often accept below-<math id="S5.p2.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\beta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>β</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\beta</annotation></semantics></math> deals, inflating agreement rates, while <span id="S5.p2.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">deepseek-r</span> and <span id="S5.p2.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">gpt-r</span> exceed <math id="S5.p2.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="94\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>94</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">94\%</annotation></semantics></math> baseline agreement.
We therefore focus on <span id="S5.p2.1.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">gemini-r</span> and <span id="S5.p2.1.6" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">grok-r</span> in this paper.
Appendix <a href="#A5" title="Appendix E Additional Quantitative Results ‣ Knowing Whom to Trust is not Enough: The Trust–Agreement Gap in Repeated Multi-Party LLM Negotiation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">E</span></a> reports results for all models (Appendices <a href="#A5.SS2" title="E.2 Complete Trust-Formation Results ‣ Appendix E Additional Quantitative Results ‣ Knowing Whom to Trust is not Enough: The Trust–Agreement Gap in Repeated Multi-Party LLM Negotiation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">E.2</span></a> and <a href="#A5.SS3" title="E.3 Complete Negotiation-Outcome Results ‣ Appendix E Additional Quantitative Results ‣ Knowing Whom to Trust is not Enough: The Trust–Agreement Gap in Repeated Multi-Party LLM Negotiation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">E.3</span></a>) and the sensitivity to <math id="S5.p2.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\lambda" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>λ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lambda</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="S5.p2.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\gamma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>γ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\gamma</annotation></semantics></math>, and <math id="S5.p2.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau_{ij}^{1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>τ</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow><mn>1</mn></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau_{ij}^{1}</annotation></semantics></math> (Appendices <a href="#A5.SS6" title="E.6 EMA Sensitivity ‣ Appendix E Additional Quantitative Results ‣ Knowing Whom to Trust is not Enough: The Trust–Agreement Gap in Repeated Multi-Party LLM Negotiation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">E.6</span></a>, <a href="#A5.SS8" title="E.8 BRS Forgetting-Factor Sensitivity ‣ Appendix E Additional Quantitative Results ‣ Knowing Whom to Trust is not Enough: The Trust–Agreement Gap in Repeated Multi-Party LLM Negotiation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">E.8</span></a>, and <a href="#A5.SS7" title="E.7 Initial-Trust Prior Sensitivity ‣ Appendix E Additional Quantitative Results ‣ Knowing Whom to Trust is not Enough: The Trust–Agreement Gap in Repeated Multi-Party LLM Negotiation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">E.7</span></a>).</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S5.p3.1" class="ltx_p">Trust-aware agents receive one of two guidance levels.
Under <em id="S5.p3.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">scores-only</em> guidance (<math id="S5.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>S</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S</annotation></semantics></math>), agents receive their trust scores and a generic definition but no instruction on how to use them.
Under <em id="S5.p3.1.2" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">prescriptive</em> guidance (<math id="S5.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S{+}P" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>P</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S{+}P</annotation></semantics></math>), they also receive an interpretation of the scores and explicit guidance on using trust in proposals and votes.
Crossing the three assessment methods with the two guidance levels gives six trust-aware conditions, which we compare with a trust-agnostic baseline.
We include all the prompts for <math id="S5.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>S</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S5.p3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S{+}P" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>P</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S{+}P</annotation></semantics></math> in Appendix <a href="#A6.SS4" title="F.4 Trust Visibility and Decision Guidance ‣ Appendix F Prompts ‣ Knowing Whom to Trust is not Enough: The Trust–Agreement Gap in Repeated Multi-Party LLM Negotiation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">F.4</span></a>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.p4" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S5.p4.1" class="ltx_p">We also evaluate three controls in both settings, all with <math id="S5.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S{+}P" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>P</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S{+}P</annotation></semantics></math> guidance and assessment disabled.
The fixed-score control <math id="S5.p4.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S_{0.5}{+}P" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>S</mi><mn>0.5</mn></msub><mo>+</mo><mi>P</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S_{0.5}{+}P</annotation></semantics></math> fixes every pairwise trust score at the prior <math id="S5.p4.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.5</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.5</annotation></semantics></math> for both models to test whether the gains of <math id="S5.p4.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S{+}P" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>P</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S{+}P</annotation></semantics></math> require informative trust.
The random-score control <math id="S5.p4.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S_{\mathrm{rand}}{+}P" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>S</mi><mi>rand</mi></msub><mo>+</mo><mi>P</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S_{\mathrm{rand}}{+}P</annotation></semantics></math> instead draws a new score for every counterpart from the uniform distribution on <math id="S5.p4.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="[0,1)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[0,1)</annotation></semantics></math> before each episode, so scores differ across counterparts and episodes but carry no information about who the adversary is.
We use the same draws for both models and both settings, so any difference between models reflects how they act on the scores, not the scores themselves.
Together with no trust, <math id="S5.p4.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S_{0.5}{+}P" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>S</mi><mn>0.5</mn></msub><mo>+</mo><mi>P</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S_{0.5}{+}P</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S5.p4.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S_{\mathrm{rand}}{+}P" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>S</mi><mi>rand</mi></msub><mo>+</mo><mi>P</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S_{\mathrm{rand}}{+}P</annotation></semantics></math> serve as the baselines.
The replay condition <math id="S5.p4.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S{\to}P" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mi>P</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S{\to}P</annotation></semantics></math>, run for <span id="S5.p4.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">grok-r</span>, gives <math id="S5.p4.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S{+}P" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>P</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S{+}P</annotation></semantics></math> agents the trust formed under <math id="S5.p4.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>S</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S</annotation></semantics></math>, which bounds the trust–agreement gap from below.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S5.T1" class="ltx_table">

<section id="S5.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">5.1 </span>Evaluation Metrics</h3>

<div id="S5.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S5.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.SS1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Trust formation metrics.</span>   Let <math id="S5.SS1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{H}=\mathcal{N}\setminus\mathcal{B}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℋ</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒩</mi><mo>∖</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℬ</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{H}=\mathcal{N}\setminus\mathcal{B}</annotation></semantics></math> denote the honest parties and <math id="S5.SS1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a\in\mathcal{B}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℬ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a\in\mathcal{B}</annotation></semantics></math> the adversary.
Trust metrics are computed from the post-episode trust vectors of honest agents. These metrics address RQ1 by measuring whether trust distinguishes the adversary from honest counterparts and how this distinction evolves across episodes.
Comparing these measures across BRS, rubric-based, and free-form assessment addresses RQ2.</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.SS1.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<ul id="S5.SS1.p2.1" class="ltx_itemize">
<li id="S5.I1.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S5.I1.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.I1.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.I1.i1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold ltx_font_italic">Detection<span id="S5.I1.i1.p1.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium">.</span></span>
<span id="S5.I1.i1.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text"><math id="S5.I1.i1.p1.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\mathrm{Det}_{i}^{e}=\mathbf{1}[\tau_{ia}^{e+1}&lt;\min_{j\in\mathcal{H}\setminus\{i\}}\tau_{ij}^{e+1}]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>Det</mi><mi>i</mi><mi>e</mi></msubsup><mo>=</mo><mn>𝟏</mn><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><msubsup><mi>τ</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>a</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>e</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msubsup><mo>&lt;</mo><msub><mi>min</mi><mrow><mi>j</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℋ</mi><mo>∖</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mi>i</mi><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></msub><msubsup><mi>τ</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>e</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{Det}_{i}^{e}=\mathbf{1}[\tau_{ia}^{e+1}&lt;\min_{j\in\mathcal{H}\setminus\{i\}}\tau_{ij}^{e+1}]</annotation></semantics></math></span> indicates whether agent <math id="S5.I1.i1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>i</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i</annotation></semantics></math> assigns the adversary <math id="S5.I1.i1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>a</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a</annotation></semantics></math> strictly less trust than every honest counterpart.
Ties count as non-detection.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S5.I1.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S5.I1.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.I1.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.I1.i2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold ltx_font_italic">Misidentification<span id="S5.I1.i2.p1.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium">.</span></span>
<span id="S5.I1.i2.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text"><math id="S5.I1.i2.p1.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\mathrm{MisID}_{i}^{e}=\frac{1}{|\mathcal{H}|-1}\sum_{j\in\mathcal{H}\setminus\{i\}}\mathbf{1}[\tau_{ij}^{e+1}&lt;\tau_{ia}^{e+1}]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>MisID</mi><mi>i</mi><mi>e</mi></msubsup><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℋ</mi><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mfrac><msub><mo>∑</mo><mrow><mi>j</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℋ</mi><mo>∖</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mi>i</mi><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></msub><mn>𝟏</mn><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><msubsup><mi>τ</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>e</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msubsup><mo>&lt;</mo><msubsup><mi>τ</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>a</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>e</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{MisID}_{i}^{e}=\frac{1}{|\mathcal{H}|-1}\sum_{j\in\mathcal{H}\setminus\{i\}}\mathbf{1}[\tau_{ij}^{e+1}&lt;\tau_{ia}^{e+1}]</annotation></semantics></math></span> is the fraction of honest parties that <math id="S5.I1.i2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>i</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i</annotation></semantics></math> ranks below the adversary.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S5.I1.i3" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S5.I1.i3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.I1.i3.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.I1.i3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold ltx_font_italic">Trust separation<span id="S5.I1.i3.p1.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium">.</span></span>
<span id="S5.I1.i3.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text"><math id="S5.I1.i3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{Sep}_{i}^{e}=\bar{\tau}_{i\mathcal{H}\setminus\{i\}}^{e+1}-\tau_{ia}^{e+1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>Sep</mi><mi>i</mi><mi>e</mi></msubsup><mo>=</mo><mrow><msubsup><mover accent="true"><mi>τ</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><mrow><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℋ</mi></mrow><mo>∖</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mi>i</mi><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><mrow><mi>e</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msubsup><mo>−</mo><msubsup><mi>τ</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>a</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>e</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msubsup></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{Sep}_{i}^{e}=\bar{\tau}_{i\mathcal{H}\setminus\{i\}}^{e+1}-\tau_{ia}^{e+1}</annotation></semantics></math></span> is the difference between mean trust in the other honest parties and trust in the adversary.</p>
</div></li>
</ul>
</div>
<figure id="S5.F2" class="ltx_figure"><object type="image/svg+xml" data="2610.31971v1/fig_trust_formation_2x3.svg" id="S5.F2.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:381/219;" width="381" height="219"></object>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Figure 2: </span><span id="S5.F2.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Adversary detection, misidentification, and trust separation in 2HB+2G scenarios.</span> Shading is 95% CI.</figcaption>
</figure>
<div id="S5.SS1.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S5.SS1.p3.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.SS1.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Negotiation outcome metrics.</span>   These metrics address the first part of RQ3 by comparing agreement, social welfare, and negotiation efficiency between trust-aware and trust-agnostic conditions.</p>
<ul id="S5.SS1.p3.2" class="ltx_itemize">
<li id="S5.I2.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S5.I2.i1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S5.I2.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.I2.i1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold ltx_font_italic">Agreement rate<span id="S5.I2.i1.p1.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium">.</span></span>
The fraction of episodes ending in a deal.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S5.I2.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S5.I2.i2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S5.I2.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.I2.i2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold ltx_font_italic">Honest surplus<span id="S5.I2.i2.p1.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium">.</span></span>
Mean honest-party utility above BATNA across all episodes, with disagreement contributing zero.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S5.I2.i3" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S5.I2.i3.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S5.I2.i3.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.I2.i3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold ltx_font_italic">HB rejection rate (HB rej.)<span id="S5.I2.i3.p1.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium">.</span></span>
Among explicit votes by honest hard bargainers on proposals that clear the voter’s own BATNA, the fraction that reject. Implicit proposer acceptance is excluded.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S5.I2.i4" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S5.I2.i4.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S5.I2.i4.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.I2.i4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold ltx_font_italic">Honest-feasible conversion (Conv.)<span id="S5.I2.i4.p1.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium">.</span></span>
Among proposals made by honest agents that clear every honest agent’s BATNA, the fraction that pass the voting rule. Feasibility is evaluated from private utilities for analysis, not revealed to the agents.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S5.I2.i5" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S5.I2.i5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.I2.i5.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.I2.i5.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold ltx_font_italic">Rounds to agreement (R/deal)<span id="S5.I2.i5.p1.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium">.</span></span>
The mean number of rounds required to reach agreement, computed over successful episodes.</p>
</div></li>
</ul>
</div>
<div id="S5.SS1.p4" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S5.SS1.p4.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.SS1.p4.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Trust–agreement gap metrics.</span>   These metrics address the second part of RQ3.
Let <math id="S5.SS1.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha_{S}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>α</mi><mi>S</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha_{S}</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="S5.SS1.p4.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha_{S+P}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>α</mi><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>P</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha_{S+P}</annotation></semantics></math>, and <math id="S5.SS1.p4.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha_{S\to P}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>α</mi><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mi>P</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha_{S\to P}</annotation></semantics></math> denote the agreement rates of the corresponding conditions, and let <math id="S5.SS1.p4.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi_{S}=(m,\varnothing)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>π</mi><mi>S</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>m</mi><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∅</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi_{S}=(m,\varnothing)</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S5.SS1.p4.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi_{S+P}=(m,I_{P})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>π</mi><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>P</mi></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>m</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>I</mi><mi>P</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi_{S+P}=(m,I_{P})</annotation></semantics></math> denote the <math id="S5.SS1.p4.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>S</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S5.SS1.p4.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S{+}P" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>P</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S{+}P</annotation></semantics></math> policies of a model <math id="S5.SS1.p4.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="m" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>m</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">m</annotation></semantics></math>; <math id="S5.SS1.p4.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha_{S}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>α</mi><mi>S</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha_{S}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S5.SS1.p4.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha_{S+P}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>α</mi><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>P</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha_{S+P}</annotation></semantics></math> estimate <math id="S5.SS1.p4.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha(\phi,\pi_{S})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>α</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>ϕ</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>π</mi><mi>S</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha(\phi,\pi_{S})</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S5.SS1.p4.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha(\phi,\pi_{S+P})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>α</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>ϕ</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>π</mi><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>P</mi></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha(\phi,\pi_{S+P})</annotation></semantics></math> for assessment method <math id="S5.SS1.p4.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\phi" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>ϕ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\phi</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
<ul id="S5.SS1.p4.2" class="ltx_itemize">
<li id="S5.I3.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S5.I3.i1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S5.I3.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.I3.i1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold ltx_font_italic">Gap lower bound<span id="S5.I3.i1.p1.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium">.</span></span>
<math id="S5.I3.i1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Delta_{S\to P}=\alpha_{S\to P}-\alpha_{S}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mi>P</mi></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>α</mi><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mi>P</mi></mrow></msub><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>α</mi><mi>S</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Delta_{S\to P}=\alpha_{S\to P}-\alpha_{S}</annotation></semantics></math>.
Since <math id="S5.I3.i1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha_{S\to P}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>α</mi><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mi>P</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha_{S\to P}</annotation></semantics></math> estimates <math id="S5.I3.i1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha_{\pi_{S}}(\phi,\pi_{S+P})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>α</mi><msub><mi>π</mi><mi>S</mi></msub></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>ϕ</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>π</mi><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>P</mi></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha_{\pi_{S}}(\phi,\pi_{S+P})</annotation></semantics></math>, Eq. (<a href="#S3.E4" title="In 3.3 Trust–Agreement Gap ‣ 3 Problem Formulation ‣ Knowing Whom to Trust is not Enough: The Trust–Agreement Gap in Repeated Multi-Party LLM Negotiation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a>) gives <math id="S5.I3.i1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Delta_{S\to P}\leq\Delta_{\mathrm{TA}}(\phi,\pi_{S})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mi>P</mi></mrow></msub><mo>≤</mo><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mi>TA</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>ϕ</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>π</mi><mi>S</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Delta_{S\to P}\leq\Delta_{\mathrm{TA}}(\phi,\pi_{S})</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S5.I3.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S5.I3.i2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S5.I3.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.I3.i2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold ltx_font_italic">Normalized gap lower bound<span id="S5.I3.i2.p1.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium">.</span></span>
<math id="S5.I3.i2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\delta_{S\to P}=\Delta_{S\to P}/(1-\alpha_{S})\leq\delta_{\mathrm{TA}}(\phi,\pi_{S})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>δ</mi><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mi>P</mi></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mi>P</mi></mrow></msub><mo>/</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>α</mi><mi>S</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≤</mo><mrow><msub><mi>δ</mi><mi>TA</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>ϕ</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>π</mi><mi>S</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\delta_{S\to P}=\Delta_{S\to P}/(1-\alpha_{S})\leq\delta_{\mathrm{TA}}(\phi,\pi_{S})</annotation></semantics></math> is the share of scores-only disagreements that the same trust avoids under prescriptive guidance.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S5.I3.i3" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S5.I3.i3.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S5.I3.i3.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.I3.i3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold ltx_font_italic">Guidance effect<span id="S5.I3.i3.p1.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium">.</span></span>
<math id="S5.I3.i3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Delta_{S+P}=\alpha_{S+P}-\alpha_{S}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>P</mi></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>α</mi><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>P</mi></mrow></msub><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>α</mi><mi>S</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Delta_{S+P}=\alpha_{S+P}-\alpha_{S}</annotation></semantics></math> is the change in agreement when agents also form their trust under prescriptive guidance.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S5.I3.i4" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S5.I3.i4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.I3.i4.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.I3.i4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold ltx_font_italic">Trust effect<span id="S5.I3.i4.p1.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium">.</span></span>
<math id="S5.I3.i4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Delta_{\mathrm{trust}}=\alpha_{S+P}-\alpha_{S\to P}=\Delta_{S+P}-\Delta_{S\to P}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mi>trust</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>α</mi><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>P</mi></mrow></msub><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>α</mi><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mi>P</mi></mrow></msub></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>P</mi></mrow></msub><mo>−</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mi>P</mi></mrow></msub></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Delta_{\mathrm{trust}}=\alpha_{S+P}-\alpha_{S\to P}=\Delta_{S+P}-\Delta_{S\to P}</annotation></semantics></math> is the part of <math id="S5.I3.i4.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Delta_{S+P}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>P</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Delta_{S+P}</annotation></semantics></math> that comes from forming trust under prescriptive guidance instead of scores-only guidance.</p>
</div></li>
</ul>
</div>
<div id="S5.SS1.p5" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S5.SS1.p5.1" class="ltx_p">For trust formation and negotiation-outcome metrics, we compute each metric separately per trajectory and report the mean and <math id="S5.SS1.p5.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="95\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>95</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">95\%</annotation></semantics></math> confidence interval across trajectories.
Differences between conditions, including <math id="S5.SS1.p5.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Delta_{S\to P}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mi>P</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Delta_{S\to P}</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="S5.SS1.p5.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Delta_{S+P}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>P</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Delta_{S+P}</annotation></semantics></math>, and <math id="S5.SS1.p5.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Delta_{\mathrm{trust}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mi>trust</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Delta_{\mathrm{trust}}</annotation></semantics></math>, are paired across seed-matched trajectories, and <math id="S5.SS1.p5.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\delta_{S\to P}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>δ</mi><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mi>P</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\delta_{S\to P}</annotation></semantics></math> uses mean agreement rates.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S5.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">5.2 </span>Trust Formation</h3>

<div id="S5.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S5.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><em id="S5.SS2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_bold ltx_font_italic">No assessment method is best for both models.</em>
In 2HB+2G, all three methods detect the adversary in <math id="S5.SS2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="82.5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>82.5</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">82.5</annotation></semantics></math>–<math id="S5.SS2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="100\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>100</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">100\%</annotation></semantics></math> of assessments by episode five (Figure <a href="#S5.F2" title="Figure 2 ‣ 5.1 Evaluation Metrics ‣ 5 Experiments and Results ‣ Knowing Whom to Trust is not Enough: The Trust–Agreement Gap in Repeated Multi-Party LLM Negotiation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a>), but their ranking depends on the model.
Free-form assessment works best for <span id="S5.SS2.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">gemini-r</span> (<math id="S5.SS2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="97.8" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>97.8</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">97.8</annotation></semantics></math>–<math id="S5.SS2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="98.1\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>98.1</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">98.1\%</annotation></semantics></math> detection) and worst for <span id="S5.SS2.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">grok-r</span> (<math id="S5.SS2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="75.1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>75.1</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">75.1</annotation></semantics></math>–<math id="S5.SS2.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="89.2\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>89.2</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">89.2\%</annotation></semantics></math>), while rubric-based assessment shows the opposite (<math id="S5.SS2.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="74.0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>74.0</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">74.0</annotation></semantics></math>–<math id="S5.SS2.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="76.9\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>76.9</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">76.9\%</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S5.SS2.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="95.5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>95.5</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">95.5</annotation></semantics></math>–<math id="S5.SS2.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="97.4\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>97.4</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">97.4\%</annotation></semantics></math>).
BRS ranks second for both models (<math id="S5.SS2.p1.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="89.5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>89.5</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">89.5</annotation></semantics></math>–<math id="S5.SS2.p1.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="95.4\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>95.4</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">95.4\%</annotation></semantics></math>) and is the only method that stays above <math id="S5.SS2.p1.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="89\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>89</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">89\%</annotation></semantics></math> in every condition, which makes it the most robust choice when the best method for a model is unknown.
Guidance has little effect: it changes detection by at most <math id="S5.SS2.p1.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="3.3" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>3.3</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3.3</annotation></semantics></math> points, with intervals that include zero, except for free-form <span id="S5.SS2.p1.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">grok-r</span>, where detection rises from <math id="S5.SS2.p1.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="75.1\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>75.1</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">75.1\%</annotation></semantics></math> to <math id="S5.SS2.p1.m16" class="ltx_Math" alttext="89.2\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>89.2</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">89.2\%</annotation></semantics></math>.
Appendix <a href="#A5.SS2" title="E.2 Complete Trust-Formation Results ‣ Appendix E Additional Quantitative Results ‣ Knowing Whom to Trust is not Enough: The Trust–Agreement Gap in Repeated Multi-Party LLM Negotiation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">E.2</span></a> reports the trust formation in the 1HB+3G scenarios and the other four models.</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.SS2.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S5.SS2.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><em id="S5.SS2.p2.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_bold ltx_font_italic">Each method separates the adversary differently.</em>
Rubric-based assessment gives the narrowest separation (<math id="S5.SS2.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.15" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.15</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.15</annotation></semantics></math> for <span id="S5.SS2.p2.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">gemini-r</span> and <math id="S5.SS2.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.24" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.24</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.24</annotation></semantics></math> for <span id="S5.SS2.p2.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">grok-r</span>), because the bounded metrics in Eq. (<a href="#S4.E6" title="In 4.1 Trust Assessment ‣ 4 The TASMAN Framework ‣ Knowing Whom to Trust is not Enough: The Trust–Agreement Gap in Repeated Multi-Party LLM Negotiation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">6</span></a>) and the EMA update limit score movement and keep adversary trust at <math id="S5.SS2.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.39" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.39</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.39</annotation></semantics></math>–<math id="S5.SS2.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.48" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.48</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.48</annotation></semantics></math>.
With this small margin, <span id="S5.SS2.p2.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">gemini-r</span> ranks an honest party below the adversary in <math id="S5.SS2.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="10.0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>10.0</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">10.0</annotation></semantics></math>–<math id="S5.SS2.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="10.7\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>10.7</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">10.7\%</annotation></semantics></math> of comparisons.
Free-form assessment gives <span id="S5.SS2.p2.1.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">gemini-r</span> the widest separation (<math id="S5.SS2.p2.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.48" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.48</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.48</annotation></semantics></math>–<math id="S5.SS2.p2.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.49" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.49</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.49</annotation></semantics></math>) by lowering adversary trust to <math id="S5.SS2.p2.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.19" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.19</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.19</annotation></semantics></math>–<math id="S5.SS2.p2.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.20" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.20</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.20</annotation></semantics></math> by episode 20.
<span id="S5.SS2.p2.1.6" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">grok-r</span> instead raises trust in all counterparts under <math id="S5.SS2.p2.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>S</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S</annotation></semantics></math>, including the adversary (<math id="S5.SS2.p2.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.62" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.62</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.62</annotation></semantics></math>), which leaves a separation of only <math id="S5.SS2.p2.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.25" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.25</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.25</annotation></semantics></math>; <math id="S5.SS2.p2.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S{+}P" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>P</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S{+}P</annotation></semantics></math> widens it to <math id="S5.SS2.p2.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.45" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.45</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.45</annotation></semantics></math>.
BRS separates the adversary mainly by raising honest trust (<math id="S5.SS2.p2.m16" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.75" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.75</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.75</annotation></semantics></math>–<math id="S5.SS2.p2.m17" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.80" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.80</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.80</annotation></semantics></math>), while adversary trust stays near the prior (<math id="S5.SS2.p2.m18" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.42" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.42</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.42</annotation></semantics></math>–<math id="S5.SS2.p2.m19" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.51" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.51</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.51</annotation></semantics></math>) because agents report far less negative evidence about the adversary than positive evidence about honest counterparts (Figure <a href="#A5.F8" title="Figure 8 ‣ E.2 Complete Trust-Formation Results ‣ Appendix E Additional Quantitative Results ‣ Knowing Whom to Trust is not Enough: The Trust–Agreement Gap in Repeated Multi-Party LLM Negotiation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">8</span></a>, Appendix <a href="#A5.SS2" title="E.2 Complete Trust-Formation Results ‣ Appendix E Additional Quantitative Results ‣ Knowing Whom to Trust is not Enough: The Trust–Agreement Gap in Repeated Multi-Party LLM Negotiation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">E.2</span></a>).</p>
</div>
<figure id="S5.T2" class="ltx_table">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table">Table 2: </span><span id="S5.T2.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Negotiation outcomes for 2HB+2G (left) and 1HB+3G (right).</span> Mixed FF rows use an adversary of the other model. Bold marks each model’s best mean among same-model conditions. Shaded rows are the baselines. <math id="S5.T2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pm" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>±</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pm</annotation></semantics></math> is the 95% CI. The outcome results of other models are in Appendix <a href="#A5.SS3" title="E.3 Complete Negotiation-Outcome Results ‣ Appendix E Additional Quantitative Results ‣ Knowing Whom to Trust is not Enough: The Trust–Agreement Gap in Repeated Multi-Party LLM Negotiation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">E.3</span></a>.</figcaption>

<section id="S5.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">5.3 </span>Negotiation Outcomes</h3>

<div id="S5.SS3.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S5.SS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><em id="S5.SS3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_bold ltx_font_italic">S+P raises agreement through voting.</em>
With <math id="S5.SS3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S{+}P" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>P</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S{+}P</annotation></semantics></math>, <span id="S5.SS3.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">grok-r</span> raises mean agreement over no trust in all six conditions, by <math id="S5.SS3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="9.0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>9.0</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">9.0</annotation></semantics></math> to <math id="S5.SS3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="23.0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>23.0</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">23.0</annotation></semantics></math> points (Table <a href="#S5.T2" title="Table 2 ‣ 5.2 Trust Formation ‣ 5 Experiments and Results ‣ Knowing Whom to Trust is not Enough: The Trust–Agreement Gap in Repeated Multi-Party LLM Negotiation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a>).
Free-form <math id="S5.SS3.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S{+}P" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>P</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S{+}P</annotation></semantics></math> adds <math id="S5.SS3.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="12.0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>12.0</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">12.0</annotation></semantics></math> points of agreement and <math id="S5.SS3.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="28\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>28</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">28\%</annotation></semantics></math> honest surplus in 2HB+2G, and free-form and BRS <math id="S5.SS3.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S{+}P" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>P</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S{+}P</annotation></semantics></math> each add <math id="S5.SS3.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="23.0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>23.0</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">23.0</annotation></semantics></math> points and <math id="S5.SS3.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="43" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>43</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">43</annotation></semantics></math>–<math id="S5.SS3.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="45\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>45</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">45\%</annotation></semantics></math> in 1HB+3G; all these paired intervals exclude zero.
Under <math id="S5.SS3.p1.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S{+}P" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>P</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S{+}P</annotation></semantics></math> in both settings, hard bargainers reject <math id="S5.SS3.p1.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="3.1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>3.1</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3.1</annotation></semantics></math> to <math id="S5.SS3.p1.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="8.9" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>8.9</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">8.9</annotation></semantics></math> points fewer of the proposals that clear their BATNA, whereas <math id="S5.SS3.p1.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>S</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S</annotation></semantics></math> changes this rate by at most <math id="S5.SS3.p1.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1.0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>1.0</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1.0</annotation></semantics></math> point.
Thus, more honest-feasible proposals pass and agreements form in fewer rounds.</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.SS3.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S5.SS3.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><em id="S5.SS3.p2.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_bold ltx_font_italic">The gains require informative trust, not guidance alone.</em>
With <math id="S5.SS3.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S{+}P" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>P</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S{+}P</annotation></semantics></math> guidance but trust fixed at <math id="S5.SS3.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.5</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.5</annotation></semantics></math> (<math id="S5.SS3.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S_{0.5}{+}P" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>S</mi><mn>0.5</mn></msub><mo>+</mo><mi>P</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S_{0.5}{+}P</annotation></semantics></math>) for every counterpart, agreement drops below the trust-agnostic baseline by <math id="S5.SS3.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="5.0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>5.0</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">5.0</annotation></semantics></math> to <math id="S5.SS3.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="5.5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>5.5</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">5.5</annotation></semantics></math> points in three of the four model-setting pairs.
Under the same guidance, updated trust exceeds fixed trust in all twelve <math id="S5.SS3.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S{+}P" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>P</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S{+}P</annotation></semantics></math> conditions, by <math id="S5.SS3.p2.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="3.5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>3.5</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3.5</annotation></semantics></math> to <math id="S5.SS3.p2.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="21.5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>21.5</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">21.5</annotation></semantics></math> points.
For <span id="S5.SS3.p2.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">grok-r</span>’s free-form trust, the gains of <math id="S5.SS3.p2.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="17.0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>17.0</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">17.0</annotation></semantics></math> points in 2HB+2G and <math id="S5.SS3.p2.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="19.5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>19.5</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">19.5</annotation></semantics></math> points in 1HB+3G have paired intervals that exclude zero.
For <span id="S5.SS3.p2.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">gemini-r</span>, fixed trust also lowers honest surplus and raises hard-bargainer rejections in both settings.
Random trust leads to the same conclusion.
With <math id="S5.SS3.p2.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S_{\mathrm{rand}}{+}P" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>S</mi><mi>rand</mi></msub><mo>+</mo><mi>P</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S_{\mathrm{rand}}{+}P</annotation></semantics></math>, agreement changes by <math id="S5.SS3.p2.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="-3.0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>3.0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-3.0</annotation></semantics></math> to <math id="S5.SS3.p2.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="10.0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>10.0</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">10.0</annotation></semantics></math> points relative to no trust, and no paired interval excludes zero.
Updated trust exceeds random trust in eleven of the twelve <math id="S5.SS3.p2.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S{+}P" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>P</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S{+}P</annotation></semantics></math> conditions, by up to <math id="S5.SS3.p2.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="19.0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>19.0</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">19.0</annotation></semantics></math> points.
The difference is largest in 1HB+3G, where free-form trust adds <math id="S5.SS3.p2.m16" class="ltx_Math" alttext="19.0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>19.0</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">19.0</annotation></semantics></math> points for <span id="S5.SS3.p2.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">gemini-r</span> and <math id="S5.SS3.p2.m17" class="ltx_Math" alttext="13.0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>13.0</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">13.0</annotation></semantics></math> points for <span id="S5.SS3.p2.1.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">grok-r</span>, and both paired intervals exclude zero.
Scores that vary but say nothing about the adversary therefore do not reproduce the gains of <math id="S5.SS3.p2.m18" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S{+}P" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>P</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S{+}P</annotation></semantics></math>.
Guidance thus helps only when trust is informative.</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.SS3.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S5.SS3.p3.1" class="ltx_p"><em id="S5.SS3.p3.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_bold ltx_font_italic">BRS performs on par with LLM-based assessments.</em>
Under the same guidance, BRS does not differ significantly from rubric-based or free-form assessment in agreement or honest surplus in <math id="S5.SS3.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="15" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>15</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">15</annotation></semantics></math> of <math id="S5.SS3.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="16" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>16</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">16</annotation></semantics></math> paired comparisons.
The exception is <span id="S5.SS3.p3.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">grok-r</span> in 1HB+3G under <math id="S5.SS3.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>S</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S</annotation></semantics></math>, where BRS has the lowest agreement of the three methods (<math id="S5.SS3.p3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="35.5\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>35.5</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">35.5\%</annotation></semantics></math>) and trails free-form assessment by <math id="S5.SS3.p3.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="9.5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>9.5</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">9.5</annotation></semantics></math> points.
Under <math id="S5.SS3.p3.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S{+}P" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>P</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S{+}P</annotation></semantics></math>, however, BRS gains <math id="S5.SS3.p3.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="33.0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>33.0</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">33.0</annotation></semantics></math> points, the largest response to guidance in Table <a href="#S5.T2" title="Table 2 ‣ 5.2 Trust Formation ‣ 5 Experiments and Results ‣ Knowing Whom to Trust is not Enough: The Trust–Agreement Gap in Repeated Multi-Party LLM Negotiation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a>, and matches free-form assessment at <math id="S5.SS3.p3.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="68.5\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>68.5</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">68.5\%</annotation></semantics></math>.
A classical reputation model that only receives LLM-reported evidence is therefore a competitive alternative to letting the LLM compute trust itself.</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.SS3.p4" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S5.SS3.p4.1" class="ltx_p"><em id="S5.SS3.p4.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_bold ltx_font_italic">The benefit of trust depends on the model.</em>
<span id="S5.SS3.p4.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">gemini-r</span> forms the most accurate trust (Section <a href="#S5.SS2" title="5.2 Trust Formation ‣ 5 Experiments and Results ‣ Knowing Whom to Trust is not Enough: The Trust–Agreement Gap in Repeated Multi-Party LLM Negotiation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5.2</span></a>) but benefits much less from it.
No <span id="S5.SS3.p4.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">gemini-r</span> trust-aware condition significantly changes agreement in 2HB+2G.
Its largest gain is <math id="S5.SS3.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="16.0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>16.0</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">16.0</annotation></semantics></math> points with free-form <math id="S5.SS3.p4.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S{+}P" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>P</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S{+}P</annotation></semantics></math> in 1HB+3G, compared with up to <math id="S5.SS3.p4.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="23.0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>23.0</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">23.0</annotation></semantics></math> points for <span id="S5.SS3.p4.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">grok-r</span>.
Accurate trust alone therefore does not determine how much a model gains.</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.SS3.p5" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S5.SS3.p5.1" class="ltx_p"><em id="S5.SS3.p5.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_bold ltx_font_italic">A <span id="S5.SS3.p5.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">grok-r</span> adversary is harder to detect than a <span id="S5.SS3.p5.1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">gemini-r</span> adversary.</em>
Together with the same-model runs, the Mixed FF <math id="S5.SS3.p5.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S{+}P" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>P</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S{+}P</annotation></semantics></math> rows of Table <a href="#S5.T2" title="Table 2 ‣ 5.2 Trust Formation ‣ 5 Experiments and Results ‣ Knowing Whom to Trust is not Enough: The Trust–Agreement Gap in Repeated Multi-Party LLM Negotiation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a> let each honest model face both adversaries under free-form <math id="S5.SS3.p5.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S{+}P" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>P</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S{+}P</annotation></semantics></math>.
Across both honest models, agents detect a <span id="S5.SS3.p5.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">gemini-r</span> adversary in <math id="S5.SS3.p5.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="96.6" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>96.6</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">96.6</annotation></semantics></math>–<math id="S5.SS3.p5.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="98.8\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>98.8</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">98.8\%</annotation></semantics></math> of assessments, but a <span id="S5.SS3.p5.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">grok-r</span> adversary in only <math id="S5.SS3.p5.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="89.2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>89.2</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">89.2</annotation></semantics></math>–<math id="S5.SS3.p5.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="96.0\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>96.0</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">96.0\%</annotation></semantics></math>.
The difference is significant in three of the four paired comparisons: <span id="S5.SS3.p5.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">grok-r</span> detects a <span id="S5.SS3.p5.1.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">gemini-r</span> adversary <math id="S5.SS3.p5.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="9.5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>9.5</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">9.5</annotation></semantics></math> points more often in 2HB+2G and <math id="S5.SS3.p5.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="5.4" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>5.4</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">5.4</annotation></semantics></math> points more often in 1HB+3G, and <span id="S5.SS3.p5.1.6" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">gemini-r</span> detects a <span id="S5.SS3.p5.1.7" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">grok-r</span> adversary <math id="S5.SS3.p5.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="6.5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>6.5</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">6.5</annotation></semantics></math> points less often in 1HB+3G.
The <span id="S5.SS3.p5.1.8" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">grok-r</span> adversary also leaves agreement lower in three of the four comparisons.
Against the <span id="S5.SS3.p5.1.9" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">gemini-r</span> adversary, honest <span id="S5.SS3.p5.1.10" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">grok-r</span> agents reach the best mean negotiation outcomes of all 2HB+2G conditions.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S5.T3" class="ltx_table">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table">Table 3: </span><span id="S5.T3.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Trust–agreement gap of <span id="S5.T3.3.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">grok-r</span>.</span> 2HB+2G (left) and 1HB+3G (right). Agreement rates <math id="S5.T3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>α</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha</annotation></semantics></math> are in %, and differences <math id="S5.T3.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Delta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Delta</annotation></semantics></math> are in points <math id="S5.T3.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pm" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>±</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pm</annotation></semantics></math> paired 95% CI; bold marks intervals that exclude zero. Shaded columns are the lower bounds on the gap.</figcaption>

<td id="S5.T3.4.2.2" class="ltx_td ltx_nopad_l ltx_nopad_r ltx_align_center ltx_border_t" style="padding-left:0.8pt;padding-right:0.8pt;">45.5</td>
<td id="S5.T3.4.2.3" class="ltx_td ltx_nopad_l ltx_nopad_r ltx_align_center ltx_border_t" style="padding-left:0.8pt;padding-right:0.8pt;">49.0</td>
<td id="S5.T3.4.2.4" class="ltx_td ltx_nopad_l ltx_nopad_r ltx_align_center ltx_border_t" style="padding-left:0.8pt;padding-right:0.8pt;">50.5</td>
