If <math id="A2.SS2.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="j" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>j</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">j</annotation></semantics></math> does not propose, <math id="A2.SS2.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="C(j)=0.5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>C</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>j</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0.5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">C(j)=0.5</annotation></semantics></math>, so the absence of a proposing
opportunity is treated as neutral evidence.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A2.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">B.3 </span>Outlier Rejection Rate</h3>

<div id="A2.SS3.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A2.SS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The outlier rejection rate measures how often <math id="A2.SS3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="j" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>j</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">j</annotation></semantics></math> rejects a proposal
without broad support from the other voters:</p>
<table id="A2.E9" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A2.E9.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="O(j)=\begin{cases}\displaystyle\frac{1}{|\mathcal{R}^{\mathrm{v}}_{j}|}\sum_{r\in\mathcal{R}^{\mathrm{v}}_{j}}\mathbf{1}[v_{j,e,r}=0]\,\mathbf{1}[q_{r}^{-j}&lt;q^{*}],&amp;|\mathcal{R}^{\mathrm{v}}_{j}|\geq s_{\min},\\[8.0pt]
0.5,&amp;|\mathcal{R}^{\mathrm{v}}_{j}|&lt;s_{\min}.\end{cases}" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>O</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>j</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mtable columnspacing="5pt" displaystyle="true" rowspacing="0pt"><mtr><mtd class="ltx_align_left" columnalign="left"><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><msubsup><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℛ</mi><mi>j</mi><mi>v</mi></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow></mfrac><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><msub><mrow></mrow><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>∈</mo><msubsup><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℛ</mi><mi>j</mi><mi>v</mi></msubsup></mrow></msub><mn>𝟏</mn><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mi>v</mi><msub><mrow></mrow><mrow><mi>j</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>e</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>r</mi></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">]</mo><mn class="ltx_mathvariant_bold" mathvariant="bold"> 1</mn><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mi>q</mi><msub><mrow></mrow><mi>r</mi></msub><msup><mrow></mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></msup><mo>&lt;</mo><mi>q</mi><msup><mrow></mrow><mo>∗</mo></msup><mo stretchy="false">]</mo><mo>,</mo></mrow></mtd><mtd class="ltx_align_left" columnalign="left"><mrow><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><msubsup><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℛ</mi><mi>j</mi><mi>v</mi></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><mo>≥</mo><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>min</mi></msub></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd class="ltx_align_left" columnalign="left"><mrow><mn>0.5</mn><mo>,</mo></mrow></mtd><mtd class="ltx_align_left" columnalign="left"><mrow><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><msubsup><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℛ</mi><mi>j</mi><mi>v</mi></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><mo>&lt;</mo><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>min</mi></msub></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow></mtd></mtr></mtable></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">O(j)=\begin{cases}\displaystyle\frac{1}{|\mathcal{R}^{\mathrm{v}}_{j}|}\sum_{r\in\mathcal{R}^{\mathrm{v}}_{j}}\mathbf{1}[v_{j,e,r}=0]\,\mathbf{1}[q_{r}^{-j}&lt;q^{*}],&amp;|\mathcal{R}^{\mathrm{v}}_{j}|\geq s_{\min},\\[8.0pt]
0.5,&amp;|\mathcal{R}^{\mathrm{v}}_{j}|&lt;s_{\min}.\end{cases}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(9)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A2.SS3.p1.2" class="ltx_p">The denominator includes every non-proposer vote cast by <math id="A2.SS3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="j" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>j</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">j</annotation></semantics></math>, including
acceptances. A rejection contributes one when fewer than <math id="A2.SS3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="q^{*}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>q</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q^{*}</annotation></semantics></math> of the other
voters also reject. With <math id="A2.SS3.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="q^{*}=2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>q</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q^{*}=2</annotation></semantics></math>, the metric counts a rejection made alone
or with exactly one other rejecter. It therefore measures rejection by a small
minority rather than only solitary rejection.</p>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS3.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A2.SS3.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Outlier rejection and counterfactual blame may count the same vote. When
exactly <math id="A2.SS3.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="q^{*}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>q</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q^{*}</annotation></semantics></math> parties reject, each rejection is decisive and is also shared
by fewer than <math id="A2.SS3.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="q^{*}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>q</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q^{*}</annotation></semantics></math> other rejecters. The two metrics nevertheless capture
different properties. <math id="A2.SS3.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="b(j)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>j</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">b(j)</annotation></semantics></math> records participation in a decisive failure,
whereas <math id="A2.SS3.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="O(j)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>O</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>j</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">O(j)</annotation></semantics></math> records how often <math id="A2.SS3.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="j" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>j</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">j</annotation></semantics></math>’s rejections lack broad support. If
<math id="A2.SS3.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="j" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>j</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">j</annotation></semantics></math> casts fewer than <math id="A2.SS3.p2.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="s_{\min}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>min</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s_{\min}</annotation></semantics></math> non-proposer votes, <math id="A2.SS3.p2.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="O(j)=0.5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>O</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>j</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0.5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">O(j)=0.5</annotation></semantics></math>, which
indicates insufficient evidence.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A2.SS4" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">B.4 </span>Targeted-Failure Rate</h3>

<div id="A2.SS4.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A2.SS4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The targeted-failure rate measures how often <math id="A2.SS4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="j" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>j</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">j</annotation></semantics></math>’s proposals fail with
exactly the minimum number of rejections:</p>
<table id="A2.E10" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A2.E10.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T(j)=\begin{cases}\displaystyle\frac{1}{|\mathcal{R}^{\mathrm{p}}_{j}|}\sum_{r\in\mathcal{R}^{\mathrm{p}}_{j}}\mathbf{1}[q_{r}=q^{*}],&amp;|\mathcal{R}^{\mathrm{p}}_{j}|&gt;0,\\[8.0pt]
0,&amp;|\mathcal{R}^{\mathrm{p}}_{j}|=0.\end{cases}" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>T</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>j</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mtable columnspacing="5pt" displaystyle="true" rowspacing="0pt"><mtr><mtd class="ltx_align_left" columnalign="left"><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><msubsup><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℛ</mi><mi>j</mi><mi>p</mi></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow></mfrac><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><msub><mrow></mrow><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>∈</mo><msubsup><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℛ</mi><mi>j</mi><mi>p</mi></msubsup></mrow></msub><mn>𝟏</mn><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mi>q</mi><msub><mrow></mrow><mi>r</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mi>q</mi><msup><mrow></mrow><mo>∗</mo></msup><mo stretchy="false">]</mo><mo>,</mo></mrow></mtd><mtd class="ltx_align_left" columnalign="left"><mrow><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><msubsup><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℛ</mi><mi>j</mi><mi>p</mi></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd class="ltx_align_left" columnalign="left"><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo></mrow></mtd><mtd class="ltx_align_left" columnalign="left"><mrow><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><msubsup><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℛ</mi><mi>j</mi><mi>p</mi></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow></mtd></mtr></mtable></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T(j)=\begin{cases}\displaystyle\frac{1}{|\mathcal{R}^{\mathrm{p}}_{j}|}\sum_{r\in\mathcal{R}^{\mathrm{p}}_{j}}\mathbf{1}[q_{r}=q^{*}],&amp;|\mathcal{R}^{\mathrm{p}}_{j}|&gt;0,\\[8.0pt]
0,&amp;|\mathcal{R}^{\mathrm{p}}_{j}|=0.\end{cases}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(10)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A2.SS4.p1.2" class="ltx_p">The numerator counts only proposals at the minimum failure margin, each of
which would pass if any one rejecter changed its vote. Proposals that receive
more than <math id="A2.SS4.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="q^{*}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>q</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q^{*}</annotation></semantics></math> rejections do not contribute to <math id="A2.SS4.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T(j)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>T</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>j</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T(j)</annotation></semantics></math> because they fail
by more than the minimum margin. If <math id="A2.SS4.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="j" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>j</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">j</annotation></semantics></math> does not propose during the episode,
<math id="A2.SS4.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T(j)=0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>T</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>j</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T(j)=0</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS4.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A2.SS4.p2.1" class="ltx_p">A high <math id="A2.SS4.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T(j)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>T</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>j</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T(j)</annotation></semantics></math> may indicate that <math id="A2.SS4.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="j" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>j</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">j</annotation></semantics></math> repeatedly proposes deals designed to
appear acceptable while remaining just short of agreement. However, the same
pattern can arise from a genuine preference conflict or from inaccurate
beliefs about the other parties. The metric identifies proposals that
repeatedly fail by the minimum margin, but it does not establish intent.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A2.SS5" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">B.5 </span>Vote–Priority Inconsistency</h3>

<div id="A2.SS5.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A2.SS5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Vote–priority inconsistency measures whether <math id="A2.SS5.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="j" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>j</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">j</annotation></semantics></math>’s votes agree with its
public rationales and known priorities. Let
<math id="A2.SS5.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="c_{ij,e,r}\in\{0,1\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>c</mi><mrow><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi>e</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>r</mi></mrow></msub><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c_{ij,e,r}\in\{0,1\}</annotation></semantics></math> equal one when assessor <math id="A2.SS5.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>i</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i</annotation></semantics></math> finds that the
available evidence supports a contradiction between <math id="A2.SS5.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="j" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>j</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">j</annotation></semantics></math>’s non-proposer
vote in round <math id="A2.SS5.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>r</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r</annotation></semantics></math> and its public rationales and known priorities, and zero
otherwise. We define</p>
<table id="A2.E11" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A2.E11.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="F(j)=\begin{cases}\displaystyle\frac{1}{|\mathcal{R}^{\mathrm{v}}_{j}|}\sum_{r\in\mathcal{R}^{\mathrm{v}}_{j}}c_{ij,e,r},&amp;|\mathcal{R}^{\mathrm{v}}_{j}|\geq s_{\min},\\[8.0pt]
0.5,&amp;|\mathcal{R}^{\mathrm{v}}_{j}|&lt;s_{\min}.\end{cases}" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>F</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>j</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mtable columnspacing="5pt" displaystyle="true" rowspacing="0pt"><mtr><mtd class="ltx_align_left" columnalign="left"><mrow><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><msubsup><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℛ</mi><mi>j</mi><mi>v</mi></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><munder><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>∈</mo><msubsup><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℛ</mi><mi>j</mi><mi>v</mi></msubsup></mrow></munder><msub><mi>c</mi><mrow><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi>e</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>r</mi></mrow></msub></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow></mtd><mtd class="ltx_align_left" columnalign="left"><mrow><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><msubsup><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℛ</mi><mi>j</mi><mi>v</mi></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><mo>≥</mo><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>min</mi></msub></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd class="ltx_align_left" columnalign="left"><mrow><mn>0.5</mn><mo>,</mo></mrow></mtd><mtd class="ltx_align_left" columnalign="left"><mrow><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><msubsup><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℛ</mi><mi>j</mi><mi>v</mi></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><mo>&lt;</mo><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>min</mi></msub></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow></mtd></mtr></mtable></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">F(j)=\begin{cases}\displaystyle\frac{1}{|\mathcal{R}^{\mathrm{v}}_{j}|}\sum_{r\in\mathcal{R}^{\mathrm{v}}_{j}}c_{ij,e,r},&amp;|\mathcal{R}^{\mathrm{v}}_{j}|\geq s_{\min},\\[8.0pt]
0.5,&amp;|\mathcal{R}^{\mathrm{v}}_{j}|&lt;s_{\min}.\end{cases}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(11)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A2.SS5.p1.2" class="ltx_p">For each vote, the assessor considers <math id="A2.SS5.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="j" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>j</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">j</annotation></semantics></math>’s public rationales in the current
episode together with the qualitative priorities in its own briefing. An
acceptance is inconsistent when the deal conflicts with this combined
evidence, and a rejection is inconsistent when the deal appears to satisfy it.
Both kinds of inconsistent vote increase <math id="A2.SS5.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="F(j)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>F</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>j</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">F(j)</annotation></semantics></math>.
The denominator includes all non-proposer votes, whether acceptances or
rejections. A vote for which the available evidence does not support a
contradiction contributes zero to the numerator but remains in the denominator;
this does not establish that the vote was made in good faith.</p>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS5.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A2.SS5.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Unlike the other four metrics, <math id="A2.SS5.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="F(j)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>F</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>j</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">F(j)</annotation></semantics></math> requires semantic interpretation
rather than counting actions. Assessors do not observe a counterpart’s private
scores or BATNA, so they judge consistency from public rationales, votes, and
stated priorities. Different assessors may therefore judge the same vote
differently. If <math id="A2.SS5.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="j" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>j</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">j</annotation></semantics></math> cast fewer than <math id="A2.SS5.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="s_{\min}=3" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>min</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s_{\min}=3</annotation></semantics></math> non-proposer votes,
<math id="A2.SS5.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="F(j)=0.5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>F</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>j</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0.5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">F(j)=0.5</annotation></semantics></math>, which indicates insufficient evidence rather than consistency or
inconsistency.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A2.SS6" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">B.6 </span>Obstruction Score and Trust Signal</h3>

<div id="A2.SS6.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A2.SS6.p1.1" class="ltx_p">After computing the five metrics, the assessing agent selects one set of
weights for all counterparts:</p>
<table id="A2.E12" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A2.E12.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="w_{1},\ldots,w_{5}\in[0,1],\qquad w_{1}+w_{2}+w_{3}+w_{4}+w_{5}=1." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>w</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><mrow><msub><mi>w</mi><mn>5</mn></msub><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="2.167em">,</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>w</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>w</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>w</mi><mn>3</mn></msub><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>w</mi><mn>4</mn></msub><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>w</mi><mn>5</mn></msub></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">w_{1},\ldots,w_{5}\in[0,1],\qquad w_{1}+w_{2}+w_{3}+w_{4}+w_{5}=1.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(12)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A2.SS6.p1.2" class="ltx_p">The weights <math id="A2.SS6.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="w_{1},\ldots,w_{5}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>w</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>w</mi><mn>5</mn></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">w_{1},\ldots,w_{5}</annotation></semantics></math> apply to <math id="A2.SS6.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="b(j)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>j</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">b(j)</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="A2.SS6.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1-C(j)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mrow><mi>C</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>j</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1-C(j)</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="A2.SS6.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="O(j)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>O</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>j</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">O(j)</annotation></semantics></math>,
<math id="A2.SS6.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T(j)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>T</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>j</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T(j)</annotation></semantics></math>, and <math id="A2.SS6.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="F(j)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>F</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>j</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">F(j)</annotation></semantics></math>, respectively. Using the same weights for every
counterpart within an assessment makes the resulting scores comparable across
parties. The weights may differ across assessors and episodes, so agents can
emphasize the evidence they consider most informative. The obstruction score
is</p>
<table id="A2.E13" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A2.E13.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{Obs}_{ij}^{e}=w_{1}b(j)+w_{2}\bigl[1-C(j)\bigr]+w_{3}O(j)+w_{4}T(j)+w_{5}F(j)." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msubsup><mi>Obs</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow><mi>e</mi></msubsup><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>w</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>b</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>j</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><msub><mi>w</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">[</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mrow><mi>C</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>j</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">]</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><msub><mi>w</mi><mn>3</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>O</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>j</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><msub><mi>w</mi><mn>4</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>T</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>j</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><msub><mi>w</mi><mn>5</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>F</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>j</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{Obs}_{ij}^{e}=w_{1}b(j)+w_{2}\bigl[1-C(j)\bigr]+w_{3}O(j)+w_{4}T(j)+w_{5}F(j).</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(13)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A2.SS6.p1.3" class="ltx_p">Because the weights are nonnegative and sum to one,
<math id="A2.SS6.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{Obs}_{ij}^{e}\in[0,1]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>Obs</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow><mi>e</mi></msubsup><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{Obs}_{ij}^{e}\in[0,1]</annotation></semantics></math>. The episode trust signal is</p>
<table id="A2.E14" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A2.E14.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="z_{ij}^{e}=1-\mathrm{Obs}_{ij}^{e}," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msubsup><mi>z</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow><mi>e</mi></msubsup><mo>=</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><msubsup><mi>Obs</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow><mi>e</mi></msubsup></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">z_{ij}^{e}=1-\mathrm{Obs}_{ij}^{e},</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(14)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A2.SS6.p1.4" class="ltx_p">and the agent updates its trust as an exponential moving average (EMA),</p>
<table id="A2.E15" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A2.E15.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau_{ij}^{e+1}=\lambda\tau_{ij}^{e}+(1-\lambda)z_{ij}^{e}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msubsup><mi>τ</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>e</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msubsup><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>λ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msubsup><mi>τ</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow><mi>e</mi></msubsup></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>λ</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msubsup><mi>z</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow><mi>e</mi></msubsup></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau_{ij}^{e+1}=\lambda\tau_{ij}^{e}+(1-\lambda)z_{ij}^{e}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(15)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A2.SS6.p1.5" class="ltx_p">The agent clips its reported trust to <math id="A2.SS6.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="[0,1]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[0,1]</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS6.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A2.SS6.p2.1" class="ltx_p">The default values reflect two forms of missing evidence. Counterfactual blame
and targeted failure default to zero when the relevant event does not occur.
Outlier rejection and vote–priority inconsistency default to <math id="A2.SS6.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.5</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.5</annotation></semantics></math> when
there are too few votes, and cooperation as proposer defaults to <math id="A2.SS6.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.5</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.5</annotation></semantics></math> when
the party never proposes. An episode with little evidence therefore need not
yield the neutral signal <math id="A2.SS6.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="z_{ij}^{e}=0.5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>z</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow><mi>e</mi></msubsup><mo>=</mo><mn>0.5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">z_{ij}^{e}=0.5</annotation></semantics></math>, because the result also depends on
the selected weights.</p>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS6.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A2.SS6.p3.1" class="ltx_p">The LLM reports the five metrics, the obstruction score, the shared weights,
one rationale for the weights, and its updated trust in each counterpart. We
use these values as reported, so this condition tests whether the LLM can
apply a specified trust model. Appendix <a href="#A6.SS8" title="F.8 Rubric-based Trust-Update Prompt ‣ Appendix F Prompts ‣ Knowing Whom to Trust is not Enough: The Trust–Agreement Gap in Repeated Multi-Party LLM Negotiation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">F.8</span></a>
gives the complete prompt.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A2.SS7" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">B.7 </span>Connection to Prior Work</h3>

<div id="A2.SS7.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A2.SS7.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The rubric draws on established ideas from causal responsibility, indirect
reciprocity, reputation systems, revealed preference, and strategic voting.
These works motivate the evidence that the five metrics capture and the way
the agent combines this evidence over time. Our definitions are nevertheless
specific to the negotiation protocol and are not direct implementations of
the cited models.</p>
</div>
<section id="A2.SS7.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Responsibility for failed proposals.</h4>

<div id="A2.SS7.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A2.SS7.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Counterfactual blame is related to the account of causal responsibility by
<cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citet"><a href="#bib.bib39" title="" class="ltx_ref">Chockler and Halpern [9]</a></cite>, which asks whether changing an action
would change an outcome. When <math id="A2.SS7.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="q_{r}=q^{*}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>q</mi><mi>r</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>q</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q_{r}=q^{*}</annotation></semantics></math>, replacing any one rejection with an
acceptance would make the proposal pass, and <math id="A2.SS7.SSS0.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="b(j)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>j</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">b(j)</annotation></semantics></math> records how often party
<math id="A2.SS7.SSS0.Px1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="j" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>j</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">j</annotation></semantics></math> is in this position. <math id="A2.SS7.SSS0.Px1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T(j)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>T</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>j</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T(j)</annotation></semantics></math> applies the same idea to <math id="A2.SS7.SSS0.Px1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="j" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>j</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">j</annotation></semantics></math>’s own
proposals that fail by the minimum margin. Our measures are observed
frequencies rather than the formal degree of responsibility of
<cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citet"><a href="#bib.bib39" title="" class="ltx_ref">Chockler and Halpern [9]</a></cite>, and neither measure establishes intent.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A2.SS7.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Cooperation and behavior-based reputation.</h4>

<div id="A2.SS7.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A2.SS7.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Models of indirect reciprocity explain how observed cooperation and defection
form reputations that influence later behavior <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib42" title="" class="ltx_ref">28</a>]</cite>.
They also show that conduct must be judged in context, because an apparent
defection can be either justified or unjustified. This motivates including
cooperation as one component of trust rather than treating every rejection as
equivalent. We measure cooperation as the mean support that <math id="A2.SS7.SSS0.Px2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="j" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>j</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">j</annotation></semantics></math>’s proposals
receive, which is specific to negotiation. <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citet"><a href="#bib.bib42" title="" class="ltx_ref">Nowak and Sigmund [28]</a></cite> study
reputations based on an actor’s own decision to cooperate or defect, whereas
<math id="A2.SS7.SSS0.Px2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="C(j)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>C</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>j</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">C(j)</annotation></semantics></math> measures how other parties respond to the actor’s proposals.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A2.SS7.SSS0.Px3" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Behavior relative to the group.</h4>

<div id="A2.SS7.SSS0.Px3.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A2.SS7.SSS0.Px3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Outlier rejection <math id="A2.SS7.SSS0.Px3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="O(j)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>O</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>j</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">O(j)</annotation></semantics></math> is motivated by work on unfair ratings in
reputation systems. <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citet"><a href="#bib.bib40" title="" class="ltx_ref">Whitby [42]</a></cite> identify ratings whose
statistical pattern differs from the prevailing distribution and filter them
out before computing reputation. Similarly, <math id="A2.SS7.SSS0.Px3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="O(j)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>O</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>j</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">O(j)</annotation></semantics></math> identifies rejections
that lack broad support from the other voters. Votes differ from reputation
reports, however, and a minority position may be justified. We therefore
retain every vote and use group behavior only as context.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A2.SS7.SSS0.Px4" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Behavioral consistency and strategic voting.</h4>

<div id="A2.SS7.SSS0.Px4.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A2.SS7.SSS0.Px4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Revealed-preference analysis asks whether observed choices can be explained
by a stable preference relation <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib38" title="" class="ltx_ref">41</a>]</cite>. This principle
motivates vote–priority inconsistency <math id="A2.SS7.SSS0.Px4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="F(j)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>F</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>j</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">F(j)</annotation></semantics></math>. Votes are observable choices,
and public rationales and known priorities provide evidence about the
preferences that these choices should reflect. Our metric is not a formal
revealed-preference test, since it neither observes feasible choice sets nor
recovers a utility function. Instead, an LLM judges whether votes are
consistent with the qualitative evidence available in the negotiation.</p>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS7.SSS0.Px4.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A2.SS7.SSS0.Px4.p2.1" class="ltx_p">An apparent inconsistency may also be strategic rather than accidental.
<cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citet"><a href="#bib.bib41" title="" class="ltx_ref">Gibbard [15]</a></cite> shows that under broad conditions voting
schemes allow agents to benefit from misrepresenting their preferences. This
result motivates treating persistent differences between stated priorities
and votes as informative. It does not make <math id="A2.SS7.SSS0.Px4.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="F(j)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>F</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>j</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">F(j)</annotation></semantics></math> a test for manipulation,
because an inconsistent vote may reflect changing beliefs, incomplete public
information, or ordinary reasoning error rather than deception.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A2.SS7.SSS0.Px5" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Combining and retaining evidence.</h4>

<div id="A2.SS7.SSS0.Px5.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A2.SS7.SSS0.Px5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">FIRE offers a related approach to aggregating trust evidence
<cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib27" title="" class="ltx_ref">18</a>]</cite>. It combines interaction trust, role-based trust,
witness reputation, and certified reputation through a weighted mean, and it
gives more influence to recent interactions.
Equations (<a href="#A2.E13" title="In B.6 Obstruction Score and Trust Signal ‣ Appendix B Rubric-Based Trust ‣ Knowing Whom to Trust is not Enough: The Trust–Agreement Gap in Repeated Multi-Party LLM Negotiation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">13</span></a>) and (<a href="#A2.E15" title="In B.6 Obstruction Score and Trust Signal ‣ Appendix B Rubric-Based Trust ‣ Knowing Whom to Trust is not Enough: The Trust–Agreement Gap in Repeated Multi-Party LLM Negotiation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">15</span></a>)
follow the same two principles. They combine several evidence dimensions into
one assessment, and they let recent behavior update rather than replace
accumulated trust. The methods differ in two respects. FIRE weights
information sources by their importance and reliability, whereas our LLM
selects <math id="A2.SS7.SSS0.Px5.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="w_{1},\ldots,w_{5}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>w</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>w</mi><mn>5</mn></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">w_{1},\ldots,w_{5}</annotation></semantics></math> for five behavioral properties of one public
transcript. FIRE also applies exponential recency weights to stored ratings
rather than the recursive EMA of Eq. (<a href="#A2.E15" title="In B.6 Obstruction Score and Trust Signal ‣ Appendix B Rubric-Based Trust ‣ Knowing Whom to Trust is not Enough: The Trust–Agreement Gap in Repeated Multi-Party LLM Negotiation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">15</span></a>). The cited work
therefore grounds the design principles of the rubric, while the metric
definitions, default values, LLM-selected weights, and temporal update remain
specific to our framework.</p>
</div>
<div class="ltx_pagination ltx_role_newpage"></div>
</section>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A3" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix C </span>Beta Reputation System (BRS)</h2>

<div id="A3.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We adapt the beta reputation system (BRS) of <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citet"><a href="#bib.bib43" title="" class="ltx_ref">Josang and Ismail [20]</a></cite> to LLM
agents. Unlike rubric-based trust, in which the LLM computes the update of
Eq. (<a href="#A2.E15" title="In B.6 Obstruction Score and Trust Signal ‣ Appendix B Rubric-Based Trust ‣ Knowing Whom to Trust is not Enough: The Trust–Agreement Gap in Repeated Multi-Party LLM Negotiation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">15</span></a>) itself, BRS limits the LLM to counting public
events and computes trust in code. After episode <math id="A3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="e" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>e</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">e</annotation></semantics></math>, each agent receives
the complete public transcript <math id="A3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H_{e}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>H</mi><mi>e</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H_{e}</annotation></semantics></math>, its current trust scores, and a
feedback rubric. For each counterpart <math id="A3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="j" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>j</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">j</annotation></semantics></math>, the agent reports the number of
positive observations <math id="A3.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="P_{ij}^{e}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>P</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow><mi>e</mi></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P_{ij}^{e}</annotation></semantics></math> and the number of negative observations
<math id="A3.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N_{ij}^{e}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>N</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow><mi>e</mi></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N_{ij}^{e}</annotation></semantics></math>, together with a short note that cites the supporting rounds.
The code then updates the evidence of the agent and computes its new trust
scores. The agent retrieves only its own scores through a read-only tool and
is instructed to use them unchanged.</p>
</div>
<section id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Feedback criteria.</h4>

<div id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The rubric asks the agent to trace the conditions that each party states and
the responses to them across public statements, proposals, and votes. It
defines two kinds of observation.</p>
<ul id="A3.I1" class="ltx_itemize">
<li id="A3.I1.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item"><math id="A3.I1.i1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bullet" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>∙</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bullet</annotation></semantics></math></span> 
<div id="A3.I1.i1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A3.I1.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><em id="A3.I1.i1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">Positive observations.</em> The party accepts an offer that meets its
own stated conditions, fulfills an applicable commitment, or makes a
consequential factual claim that the record verifies. A concrete change or an
explained compromise that addresses the concern of another party also counts
when that party confirms it through its vote or public explanation.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A3.I1.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;padding-top:2.0pt;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item"><math id="A3.I1.i2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bullet" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>∙</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bullet</annotation></semantics></math></span> 
<div id="A3.I1.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.I1.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><em id="A3.I1.i2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">Negative observations.</em> The party introduces a conflicting
blocker without explanation after its objection has been addressed. For
example, it requires option X, rejects X in favor of Y once X is offered, and
then promotes X again. The party may also give conflicting acceptance guidance
on the same deal without explanation, as when “change X and I will accept”
later becomes “Y is also essential.” Finally, the party may reject a deal on
grounds that contradict its earlier explicit endorsement, break an applicable
commitment, reverse an explicit vote on the same deal without a relevant
explanation, or make a consequential factual claim that the record
contradicts.</p>
</div></li>
</ul>
<p id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.2" class="ltx_p">The rubric also states what does not count. Firmness, rejections, repeated
proposals, and unmet demands alone are not negative observations. Repeated
demands, polite language, and routine descriptions of a deal alone are not
positive observations. The agent counts each distinct event once, ignores the
automatic acceptance of the proposer, and relies on public evidence rather
than its private utility, its prior trust, or inferred motives. When neither
kind of observation is supported, it reports <math id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="P_{ij}^{e}=N_{ij}^{e}=0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>P</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow><mi>e</mi></msubsup><mo>=</mo><msubsup><mi>N</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow><mi>e</mi></msubsup><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P_{ij}^{e}=N_{ij}^{e}=0</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Evidence update.</h4>

<div id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The code first normalizes the counts of each episode:</p>
<table id="A3.E16" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A3.E16.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bigl(\hat{\rho}_{ij}^{e},\hat{\sigma}_{ij}^{e}\bigr)=\begin{cases}\displaystyle\biggl(\frac{P_{ij}^{e}}{P_{ij}^{e}+N_{ij}^{e}},\ \frac{N_{ij}^{e}}{P_{ij}^{e}+N_{ij}^{e}}\biggr),&amp;P_{ij}^{e}+N_{ij}^{e}&gt;0,\\[10.0pt]
(0,0),&amp;P_{ij}^{e}+N_{ij}^{e}=0.\end{cases}" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">(</mo><msubsup><mover accent="true"><mi>ρ</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow><mi>e</mi></msubsup><mo>,</mo><msubsup><mover accent="true"><mi>σ</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow><mi>e</mi></msubsup><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mtable columnspacing="5pt" displaystyle="true" rowspacing="0pt"><mtr><mtd class="ltx_align_left" columnalign="left"><mrow><mrow><mo maxsize="2.100em" minsize="2.100em">(</mo><mfrac><msubsup><mi>P</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow><mi>e</mi></msubsup><mrow><msubsup><mi>P</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow><mi>e</mi></msubsup><mo>+</mo><msubsup><mi>N</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow><mi>e</mi></msubsup></mrow></mfrac><mo>,</mo><mfrac><msubsup><mi>N</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow><mi>e</mi></msubsup><mrow><msubsup><mi>P</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow><mi>e</mi></msubsup><mo>+</mo><msubsup><mi>N</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow><mi>e</mi></msubsup></mrow></mfrac><mo maxsize="2.100em" minsize="2.100em">)</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow></mtd><mtd class="ltx_align_left" columnalign="left"><mrow><mrow><mrow><msubsup><mi>P</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow><mi>e</mi></msubsup><mo>+</mo><msubsup><mi>N</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow><mi>e</mi></msubsup></mrow><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd class="ltx_align_left" columnalign="left"><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow></mtd><mtd class="ltx_align_left" columnalign="left"><mrow><mrow><mrow><msubsup><mi>P</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow><mi>e</mi></msubsup><mo>+</mo><msubsup><mi>N</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow><mi>e</mi></msubsup></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow></mtd></mtr></mtable></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bigl(\hat{\rho}_{ij}^{e},\hat{\sigma}_{ij}^{e}\bigr)=\begin{cases}\displaystyle\biggl(\frac{P_{ij}^{e}}{P_{ij}^{e}+N_{ij}^{e}},\ \frac{N_{ij}^{e}}{P_{ij}^{e}+N_{ij}^{e}}\biggr),&amp;P_{ij}^{e}+N_{ij}^{e}&gt;0,\\[10.0pt]
(0,0),&amp;P_{ij}^{e}+N_{ij}^{e}=0.\end{cases}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(16)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.2" class="ltx_p">An episode with evidence therefore contributes exactly one unit of evidence.
The number of reported observations changes the balance between positive and
negative evidence but not the weight of the episode. Let <math id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rho_{ij}^{e}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>ρ</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow><mi>e</mi></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rho_{ij}^{e}</annotation></semantics></math> and
<math id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma_{ij}^{e}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>σ</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow><mi>e</mi></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma_{ij}^{e}</annotation></semantics></math> be the accumulated positive and negative evidence of agent
<math id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>i</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i</annotation></semantics></math> about counterpart <math id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="j" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>j</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">j</annotation></semantics></math>, with <math id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rho_{ij}^{1}=\sigma_{ij}^{1}=0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>ρ</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow><mn>1</mn></msubsup><mo>=</mo><msubsup><mi>σ</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow><mn>1</mn></msubsup><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rho_{ij}^{1}=\sigma_{ij}^{1}=0</annotation></semantics></math>. After
each episode, the code discounts past evidence by the forgetting factor
<math id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\gamma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>γ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\gamma</annotation></semantics></math> and adds the new evidence:</p>
<table id="A3.E17" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A3.E17.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rho_{ij}^{e+1}=\gamma\rho_{ij}^{e}+\hat{\rho}_{ij}^{e},\qquad\sigma_{ij}^{e+1}=\gamma\sigma_{ij}^{e}+\hat{\sigma}_{ij}^{e}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msubsup><mi>ρ</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>e</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msubsup><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>γ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msubsup><mi>ρ</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow><mi>e</mi></msubsup></mrow><mo>+</mo><msubsup><mover accent="true"><mi>ρ</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow><mi>e</mi></msubsup></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="2.167em">,</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>σ</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>e</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msubsup><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>γ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msubsup><mi>σ</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow><mi>e</mi></msubsup></mrow><mo>+</mo><msubsup><mover accent="true"><mi>σ</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow><mi>e</mi></msubsup></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rho_{ij}^{e+1}=\gamma\rho_{ij}^{e}+\hat{\rho}_{ij}^{e},\qquad\sigma_{ij}^{e+1}=\gamma\sigma_{ij}^{e}+\hat{\sigma}_{ij}^{e}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(17)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.3" class="ltx_p">We use <math id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\gamma=0.9" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>γ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.9</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\gamma=0.9</annotation></semantics></math>. The discount applies after every episode, including an
episode without evidence, so old evidence fades even when an episode provides
no new observations. Trust is the mean of
<math id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{Beta}(\rho_{ij}^{e+1}+1,\sigma_{ij}^{e+1}+1)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>Beta</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>ρ</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>e</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msubsup><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>σ</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>e</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msubsup><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{Beta}(\rho_{ij}^{e+1}+1,\sigma_{ij}^{e+1}+1)</annotation></semantics></math>, which corresponds
to a uniform prior:</p>
<table id="A3.E18" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A3.E18.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau_{ij}^{e+1}=\frac{\rho_{ij}^{e+1}+1}{\rho_{ij}^{e+1}+\sigma_{ij}^{e+1}+2}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msubsup><mi>τ</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>e</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msubsup><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><msubsup><mi>ρ</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>e</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msubsup><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mrow><msubsup><mi>ρ</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>e</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msubsup><mo>+</mo><msubsup><mi>σ</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>e</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msubsup><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></mfrac></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau_{ij}^{e+1}=\frac{\rho_{ij}^{e+1}+1}{\rho_{ij}^{e+1}+\sigma_{ij}^{e+1}+2}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(18)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
<div id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p2.1" class="ltx_p">The evidence totals <math id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rho_{ij}^{e}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>ρ</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow><mi>e</mi></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rho_{ij}^{e}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma_{ij}^{e}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>σ</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow><mi>e</mi></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma_{ij}^{e}</annotation></semantics></math> are internal state
of the BRS estimator, retained to compute subsequent trust updates. They are
not supplied to the negotiating LLM. The trust vector is the only historical
information passed from earlier episodes into its negotiation decisions;
earlier transcripts and private scratchpads are not carried into that context.
Thus, the main paper’s description of trust as cross-episode state concerns
the information available to the negotiating LLM, while BRS separately
maintains the evidence needed for its update rule.</p>
</div>
<div id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p3.1" class="ltx_p">Before any evidence, trust equals <math id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.5</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.5</annotation></semantics></math>, the same initial value as in the
other two methods. Because each episode adds at most one unit of evidence and
older evidence decays by <math id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\gamma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>γ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\gamma</annotation></semantics></math>, the total evidence
<math id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rho_{ij}^{e}+\sigma_{ij}^{e}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>ρ</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow><mi>e</mi></msubsup><mo>+</mo><msubsup><mi>σ</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow><mi>e</mi></msubsup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rho_{ij}^{e}+\sigma_{ij}^{e}</annotation></semantics></math> stays below <math id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1/(1-\gamma)=10" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>γ</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>10</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1/(1-\gamma)=10</annotation></semantics></math>. BRS trust
therefore remains strictly between <math id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p3.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1/12" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>12</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1/12</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p3.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="11/12" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>11</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>12</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">11/12</annotation></semantics></math>. If the feedback of
an agent remains invalid after one correction request, or the provider blocks
the response, the code keeps the accumulated evidence of that agent unchanged
for the episode.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px3" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Relation to the original BRS.</h4>

<div id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">As in the original BRS, trust is the mean of a Beta distribution over
positive and negative evidence, and a forgetting factor discounts older
evidence. In our setting, the LLM supplies the feedback from the public
transcript. Each agent also keeps its own private evidence about each
counterpart rather than combining feedback from other agents.</p>
</div>
<div class="ltx_pagination ltx_role_newpage"></div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A4" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix D </span>Free-Form Trust Criteria and Declared Weights</h2>

<div id="A4.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">After each free-form assessment, the agent names the criteria it used and
assigns each an approximate weight, with one weight vector for all
counterparts (Appendix <a href="#A6.SS9" title="F.9 Free-Form Trust-Update Prompt ‣ Appendix F Prompts ‣ Knowing Whom to Trust is not Enough: The Trust–Agreement Gap in Repeated Multi-Party LLM Negotiation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">F.9</span></a>). Because agents
choose their own terms, we map each criterion label to one of eight behavioral
categories or to <em id="A4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">Other</em> with a fixed coding dictionary. The categories
are behavioral consistency, honesty and credibility, compromise and
flexibility, constructive proposals, obstruction and holdout, alignment with
the assessor’s own interests, communication and responsiveness, and
contribution to agreement. When a label matches more than one category, its
weight is divided equally among them. We normalize each weight vector and
average it over honest assessors within each episode, over episodes within
each trajectory, and over the 10 trajectories of each condition. We report
these shares for all six model configurations of Table 1 in the main paper,
under <math id="A4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>S</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A4.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S+P" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>P</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S+P</annotation></semantics></math> in the 2HB+2G scenarios. A valid weight vector is
available for 99.4–100% of honest assessments, and missing vectors are not
imputed.</p>
</div>
<section id="A4.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">D.1 </span>Consistency and Compromise Receive the Largest Weights</h3>

<div id="A4.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A4.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Figure <a href="#A4.F5" title="Figure 5 ‣ D.1 Consistency and Compromise Receive the Largest Weights ‣ Appendix D Free-Form Trust Criteria and Declared Weights ‣ Knowing Whom to Trust is not Enough: The Trust–Agreement Gap in Repeated Multi-Party LLM Negotiation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5</span></a> reports the declared weights
for every model. Consistency receives the largest share in every model and
guidance condition, from 38.2% for <span id="A4.SS1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">gemini-r</span> under <math id="A4.SS1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>S</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S</annotation></semantics></math> to 61.7%
for <span id="A4.SS1.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">grok-nr</span> under <math id="A4.SS1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>S</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S</annotation></semantics></math>. Compromise is the second-largest category in
every case, with 16.5–34.7% of the weight. Together, the two categories
receive 68.2–80.3% of the declared weight. Obstruction receives at most
4.9%, so agents reward cooperative behavior rather than penalize rejections.</p>
</div>
<figure id="A4.F5" class="ltx_figure"><object type="image/svg+xml" data="2610.31971v1/fig_freeform_criteria_all_models.svg" id="A4.F5.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_square" style="aspect-ratio:476/420;" width="476" height="420"></object>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Figure 5: </span><span id="A4.F5.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Declared free-form trust criteria for all models.</span> Each bar
shows the mean share of declared weight that honest assessors give each
category under <math id="A4.F5.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>S</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S</annotation></semantics></math> or <math id="A4.F5.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S+P" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>P</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S+P</annotation></semantics></math>.</figcaption>
</figure>
<div id="A4.SS1.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A4.SS1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">The remaining weight reveals model-specific emphases. <span id="A4.SS1.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">deepseek-r</span>
gives honesty and credibility 17.6% of its weight under <math id="A4.SS1.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>S</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S</annotation></semantics></math> and 20.5%
under <math id="A4.SS1.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S+P" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>P</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S+P</annotation></semantics></math>, more than any other model. <span id="A4.SS1.p2.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">grok-nr</span> is the only other
model that gives honesty more than 8% (8.8% and 11.0%). Constructive
proposals receive 7.7–12.3% for <span id="A4.SS1.p2.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">gemini-r</span>, <span id="A4.SS1.p2.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">grok-r</span>, and
<span id="A4.SS1.p2.1.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">gpt-r</span>, but at most 5.3% for the other three models.
<span id="A4.SS1.p2.1.6" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">gpt-r</span> also gives communication 8.5% under <math id="A4.SS1.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>S</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S</annotation></semantics></math> and 5.6% under
<math id="A4.SS1.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S+P" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>P</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S+P</annotation></semantics></math>. Only <span id="A4.SS1.p2.1.7" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">gemini-r</span> names criteria that reward alignment with its
own interests, and their share falls from 10.8% under <math id="A4.SS1.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>S</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S</annotation></semantics></math> to 4.6% under
<math id="A4.SS1.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S+P" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>P</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S+P</annotation></semantics></math>. The <em id="A4.SS1.p2.1.8" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">Other</em> share is at most 7.0%, so the eight categories
cover most of the declared weight. These shares describe what agents report
considering, not whether the stated criteria determine each trust judgment.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A4.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">D.2 </span>Reported Criteria Under <math id="A4.SS2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>S</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A4.SS2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S+P" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>P</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S+P</annotation></semantics></math></h3>

<div id="A4.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A4.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">For each model, we compare the <math id="A4.SS2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S+P" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>P</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S+P</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A4.SS2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>S</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S</annotation></semantics></math> conditions trajectory by
trajectory and pair the trajectories that share a seed. Each condition
produced its own negotiation history, so these differences describe the two
conditions rather than the isolated effect of guidance. We test each of the
48 model–category differences (six models and eight categories, excluding
<em id="A4.SS2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">Other</em>) with a two-sided paired <math id="A4.SS2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>t</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math>-test and apply Holm’s correction.
Because the shares sum to 100%, an increase in one category necessarily
lowers others, so we do not interpret each difference in isolation.</p>
</div>
<div id="A4.SS2.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A4.SS2.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Under <math id="A4.SS2.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S+P" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>P</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S+P</annotation></semantics></math>, <span id="A4.SS2.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">gemini-r</span>, <span id="A4.SS2.p2.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">gpt-r</span>, and <span id="A4.SS2.p2.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">gpt-nr</span> give
consistency 6.6, 10.1, and 6.3 percentage points more weight and give
compromise 2.9, 4.0, and 4.8 points less. All six differences remain
significant after correction. <span id="A4.SS2.p2.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">deepseek-r</span> moves in the same direction,
but its differences are not significant. <span id="A4.SS2.p2.1.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">grok-r</span> moves in the
opposite direction, with 2.8 points less consistency and 4.8 points more
compromise, although neither difference is significant after correction.
<span id="A4.SS2.p2.1.6" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">grok-nr</span> keeps nearly the same consistency share, with a difference
of <math id="A4.SS2.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="-0.1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>0.1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-0.1</annotation></semantics></math> points.</p>
</div>
<div id="A4.SS2.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A4.SS2.p3.1" class="ltx_p">The other significant differences are smaller. Under <math id="A4.SS2.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S+P" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>P</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S+P</annotation></semantics></math>,
<span id="A4.SS2.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">gemini-r</span> gives 6.2 fewer points to its own interests and 2.2 more
points to obstruction, and <span id="A4.SS2.p3.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">grok-nr</span> gives 3.0 more points to
obstruction. Communication falls by 1.7–2.9 points for <span id="A4.SS2.p3.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">gpt-r</span>,
<span id="A4.SS2.p3.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">gpt-nr</span>, and <span id="A4.SS2.p3.1.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">grok-r</span>, and honesty rises by 2.6 points for
<span id="A4.SS2.p3.1.6" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">gpt-nr</span>. In total, 13 of the 48 differences remain significant after
correction.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A4.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">D.3 </span>Agents Revise Their Criteria Between Episodes</h3>

<div id="A4.SS3.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A4.SS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Agents name 3.4–4.0 criteria per assessment on average, and <math id="A4.SS3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S+P" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>P</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S+P</annotation></semantics></math> changes
this number by at most 0.06 for every model. The criteria themselves change
from episode to episode. An agent’s allocation across categories differs
between consecutive episodes in 97.1–99.9% of cases, and on average
26.8–35.4% of its weight moves to different categories. The exact criterion
labels change even more often, in at least 99.8% of consecutive assessments.
Unlike the fixed rubric of Appendix <a href="#A2" title="Appendix B Rubric-Based Trust ‣ Knowing Whom to Trust is not Enough: The Trust–Agreement Gap in Repeated Multi-Party LLM Negotiation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">B</span></a>, free-form
criteria therefore adapt to what the agent observed in each episode. This
flexibility also makes free-form trust depend on the model’s own judgment.</p>
</div>
<div class="ltx_pagination ltx_role_newpage"></div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A5" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix E </span>Additional Quantitative Results</h2>

<div id="A5.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">This appendix reports the complete quantitative evidence supporting the
condensed results in the main paper. Each completed
condition contains 10 independent seeds and 200 episodes. We compute each
metric separately for each seed and report the mean and <math id="A5.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="95\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>95</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">95\%</annotation></semantics></math> confidence
interval across seeds.</p>
</div>
<section id="A5.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">E.1 </span>Seed Generation</h3>

<div id="A5.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A5.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We use base seed 42 and derive trajectory, episode, and model-call seeds
hierarchically from the first 32 bits of SHA-256 over compact JSON containing a
namespace and its parent identifiers. Episode seeds also include the episode
position and scenario-file hash; call seeds include the agent, round, and call
role. All conditions use the same fixed S01–S20 order and trajectory seeds, so
comparisons are seed-matched.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A5.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">E.2 </span>Complete Trust-Formation Results</h3>

<div id="A5.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A5.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Figure <a href="#A5.F6" title="Figure 6 ‣ E.2 Complete Trust-Formation Results ‣ Appendix E Additional Quantitative Results ‣ Knowing Whom to Trust is not Enough: The Trust–Agreement Gap in Repeated Multi-Party LLM Negotiation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">6</span></a> reports trust formation of
<span id="A5.SS2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">gemini-r</span> and <span id="A5.SS2.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">grok-r</span> in 1HB+3G scenarios.
Figure <a href="#A5.F7" title="Figure 7 ‣ E.2 Complete Trust-Formation Results ‣ Appendix E Additional Quantitative Results ‣ Knowing Whom to Trust is not Enough: The Trust–Agreement Gap in Repeated Multi-Party LLM Negotiation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">7</span></a> reports trust formation of the other
models in 2HB+2G scenarios. Figure <a href="#A5.F8" title="Figure 8 ‣ E.2 Complete Trust-Formation Results ‣ Appendix E Additional Quantitative Results ‣ Knowing Whom to Trust is not Enough: The Trust–Agreement Gap in Repeated Multi-Party LLM Negotiation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">8</span></a>
separates trust in honest peers from trust in the adversary for all models.</p>
</div>

<section id="A5.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">E.3 </span>Complete Negotiation-Outcome Results</h3>

</div>

<td id="A5.T6.4.2.6" class="ltx_td ltx_nopad_r ltx_align_center ltx_border_t" style="padding-left:0.8pt;padding-right:0.8pt;"><span id="A5.T6.4.2.6.1" class="ltx_text">94.5<math id="A5.T6.m18" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pm" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>±</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pm</annotation></semantics></math>3.1</span></td>
